payload.text:
Radial-velocity dataset seed503_diff2.

- 80 observations over a baseline of 192.1 days
- median reported uncertainty: 0.598 m/s
- instruments: instA
- host star mass: 0.849 solar masses
- submission attempts available: 3

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Initial hypothesis: 1 planet at 68.61 d.

Why:
- The 68.61 d peak is overwhelmingly dominant (power 0.875, FAP ~ 0) and is not a spectral-window feature.
- The 34.93 d peak is very likely the first harmonic / half-period relative of 68.61 d, since it lies almost exactly at half the main period and is weaker.
- The short-period peaks near 1.18 d, 0.61 d, 0.98 d, etc. are plausible aliases/harmonics from cadence and from the strong main signal, and none is comparably compelling.
- 137.2 d is the double-period relative of the main peak; with a 192 d baseline it is less directly preferred than 68.6 d.
- No peak beyond this is strong enough yet to justify a second planet before fitting the simplest model.

Please fit a 1-planet Keplerian starting from P ≈ 68.61 d, then inspect residuals to see whether any non-alias signal survives.

HANDOFF: engineer
